plan.title: AI file analysis: an opt-in documents.analysis.mode flag that replaces embedded extraction with Claude or ChatGPT (subscription or API key)

sources.title: ADR 0026: AI providers, ask and ai

context.summary: Today every document is analysed in-process: docling.rs, the PDF text layer and ocrs OCR produce Docling JSON behind the DocumentConverter trait. The normalizer, the deterministic chunker and DocumentMetadata then turn it into rows, and the knowledge linker matches chunk text to code. The goal is one switch, documents.analysis.mode: native | ai, shaped like storage.mode/storage.server.engine. With ai, the whole document analysis is bypassed and done by a cloud model: structure, chunks, metadata, summary, keywords and references to code. The model runs on a Claude subscription (the official claude CLI), a ChatGPT subscription (the official codex runtime), ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY. Code files keep the native code-intelligence path. A file whose AI analysis fails is failed and never falls back to native extraction.

baseline.metric: AI providers usable by docmonk ask
baseline.scope: openai, anthropic, openai_compatible, ollama, codex, github_copilot

baseline.metric: Cold index of 600 mixed documents, native extraction

baseline.value: native only (docling.rs + PDF text layer + ocrs)

findings.summary: The document converter is hard-wired to DoclingConverter in registry_with. There is no seam for selecting another analysis path from config.

evidence.note: DocumentConverter returns Docling JSON only, which forces the native normalizer and chunker downstream

findings.summary: Chunking, metadata and titles are always derived by the native chunker and DocumentMetadata. A processor cannot supply its own chunks, summary or keywords.

evidence.note: rows() always calls chunk_document over the normalized document

findings.summary: There is no Claude subscription provider. ChatGPT subscription exists only for answering (codex), not for analysing files, and no provider accepts file input.

evidence.note: AiProvider::answer takes an evidence AiRequest only

findings.summary: The build identity (converter_version) only describes docling and attachments. Switching the analysis path or model would leave stale rows unless the identity covers it.
The knowledge linker links code only by matching chunk text, so references a model identifies (for example a described service or route) are not used.

do_not_duplicate.summary: Reuse the privacy gate, url_host/is_local_host and the not_configured/privacy_blocked error classes. Do not add a second egress check.
Reuse the HTTP clients, error-message shapes and the recorded-exchange golden harness for the API-key providers.
Reuse the codex app-server JSON-RPC transport and the copilot CLI child-process pattern (fixed executable name on PATH, credential env stripped) for the subscription runtimes.
Reuse ConversionCache (content hash plus key) for AI results, the existing max_pages and email-attachment limits, and the tokenizer for chunk budget checks.
The config section!/one_of machinery and the DOCMONK_<SECTION>__ env layer already give the flag a YAML, env and `docmonk config set` surface.

rules: Branch from the latest main after every depends_on package is merged.
Keep provider work (E3-E6) separate from pipeline work (E7-E8) so each can be reviewed alone.
Keep the work package id in every PR title.

protected_paths.reason: Held-out labels judge the code; a model must not approve its own labels.
Floors only move up. AI mode must not get its own lower floors on the native gates.
Native extraction output must stay byte-identical when documents.analysis.mode=native.
Audits are never weakened to get CI green.

principles: Off by default: documents.analysis.mode defaults to native, and with native every byte of output, identity and every fixture is unchanged.

One flag selects the path, shaped like storage.mode/storage.server.engine: documents.analysis.mode (native | ai) plus documents.analysis.provider. It is settable in YAML, as DOCMONK_DOCUMENTS__ANALYSIS__MODE and with docmonk config set.

Full bypass for documents: with ai, docling.rs, the PDF text layer, OCR, the normalizer, the chunker and DocumentMetadata are not run on that file. The model returns structure, chunks, metadata, summary, keywords and code references. Only light, non-analysing guards stay native: format detection, size and page limits, the token budget split and schema validation.
No native fallback: a file whose AI analysis fails is recorded as failed with an ai_analysis_* code, and nothing native is indexed for it.

Privacy first: every AI analysis provider needs privacy.external_ai_allowed=true. The check runs once before the index run starts, which then exits with the policy class and code 8, so a blocked run never sends a byte.

Secrets never live in config: API keys come from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY, and subscriptions use only the official runtime's own sign-in. API-key variables are stripped from subscription child processes, so a subscription is never silently billed as API usage.
Subscriptions only through official clients: Claude through the claude CLI, ChatGPT through the codex runtime. Never read, copy or replay their OAuth tokens.
Repeat runs are reproducible: every AI result is cached by content hash and analysis identity, so re-indexing an unchanged file makes no model call and yields identical rows.
Citations stay honest: every AI-produced document and chunk records extracted_by (provider:model), and status, search output and the Admin UI show it.
Record design decisions as ADR 0045 in docs/adr/.
non_goals: No AI analysis of code files. Symbols, call graphs, routes, messaging topology and implementation passages stay native.
No fallback to native extraction when the AI fails (the user decided: fail the file).
No use of a subscription outside its official client, no token extraction, no unofficial endpoints.
No local model (Ollama) or Copilot for analysis in this plan. Both can be added later behind the same flag.
No change to the native pipeline, its fixtures or its gates.
No per-source analysis mode in this plan. The flag is global, like storage.mode (see D6).

test.purpose: Workspace tests with pinned models required, as in CI.

requires.description: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and/or OPENAI_API_KEY for the API-key cases
A signed-in claude CLI (Claude Pro/Max) and/or a signed-in codex runtime (ChatGPT plan) for the subscription cases

validate_plan.purpose: Validate this plan against its schema after every edit; then re-check x-integrity-rules by reading.

objectives.objective: One flag switches document analysis from embedded extraction to AI analysis, with nothing changed for users who leave it off.
success_criteria: documents.analysis.mode: native | ai is validated with the same one_of rule as storage.mode, defaults to native, and is settable in YAML, by env and with docmonk config set.
With native, all existing fixtures, identities and benchmarks are unchanged.
Switching the mode, provider or model changes converter_version, so every document rebuilds on the next index.

objectives.objective: Claude and ChatGPT can analyse files with either a subscription or an API key.
success_criteria: Four analysis providers: anthropic (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), openai (OPENAI_API_KEY), claude_code (Claude Pro/Max through the claude CLI) and codex (ChatGPT plan through the codex runtime).
docmonk ai providers lists which providers can analyse files and with which auth mode; docmonk ai status/login/logout work for claude_code.
claude_code is also available to docmonk ask.

objectives.objective: AI-analysed documents are first-class in search, explore, ask, citations and document-to-code links.
success_criteria: Every chunk is stored with heading path, pages (PDF), kind, table rows, and the embedding text the model wrote, within the embedding token budget.
Documents carry the model's title, author, language, summary and keywords. Search shows extracted_by.
Code references the model proposes become links only when they resolve to an existing code entity.

objectives.objective: Failures, cost and privacy are visible and controlled.
success_criteria: A failed file is recorded with an ai_analysis_* code and message in docmonk status, and nothing native is indexed for it.
An unchanged file never triggers a second model call (cache hit).
A run with external AI disallowed refuses before contacting any provider.

work_packages.title: ADR 0045 and the documents.analysis flag
work_packages.purpose: Fix the user-visible contract before code: one flag, its settings, privacy behaviour, identity and failure semantics.

tasks.title: Write ADR 0045
tasks.details: Cover: the flag and its shape (mirrors storage.mode + storage.server.engine); the full bypass for documents; the four providers and their auth; the privacy gate at run start; no native fallback; the identity and cache; extracted_by provenance; the D1-D6 decisions; and the subscription terms (official clients only).

tasks.title: Add DocumentsConfig.analysis
tasks.details: New section AnalysisConfig under documents: mode (native|ai, default native, one_of), provider (anthropic|openai|claude_code|codex, required when mode=ai), model (empty = provider default), timeout_seconds (default 300, > 0), max_file_bytes (default 32 MiB, > 0), concurrency (default 2, 1..=16), max_output_tokens (default 16000). No key fields; the doc comment says where keys come from. Validation: mode=ai without provider is a config error naming `docmonk config set documents.analysis.provider`.

tasks.title: Config tests and reference docs
tasks.details: Unit tests for defaults, the env layer (DOCMONK_DOCUMENTS__ANALYSIS__MODE=ai), bad values and the missing-provider error. Document every key in docs/reference.md.

acceptance.criterion: With the section absent or mode=native, the merged config dump and every fixture are unchanged.
ADR 0045 is merged with the owner's decisions recorded.

work_packages.rollback: Revert the PR; the section is new and defaults to native.

work_packages.title: AI document analysis schema and row mapping
work_packages.purpose: One provider-neutral contract for what a model returns for a file, and one deterministic mapping from it to DocumentRow/ChunkRow.

tasks.title: Define the analysis JSON schema
tasks.details: AnalysisResult { schema_version, title, author, language, summary, keywords[], page_count, chunks[] { kind: heading|text|table|list|caption, heading_path[], heading_level, page_start, page_end, text, embedding_text, table_rows }, code_references[] { kind: symbol|path|route|topic, value, chunk_index, quote } }. Ship it as a JSON Schema constant so providers can request structured output.

tasks.title: Analysis prompt
tasks.details: A fixed system prompt plus a per-file instruction: verbatim text only (no paraphrase in text, paraphrase allowed only in embedding_text and summary), reading order, headings as heading_path, pages for paged formats, tables as rows, and code references only when named in the file. Prompt text is hashed into the identity (E7).

tasks.title: Validator and mapper
tasks.details: Parse and validate strictly: unknown schema_version, empty chunks, page numbers outside 1..=page_count and invalid kinds are rejected with ai_analysis_invalid_output. Map to DocumentRow/ChunkRow; ids come from record::document_id/chunk_id; search_text uses the existing lexical normalization. Any chunk over the embedding token budget is split by the existing tokenizer (decision D3). The language falls back to detect_language when the model gives none.

tasks.title: Golden mapping fixtures
tasks.details: fixtures/ai_analysis/*.json: recorded model outputs (good, oversized chunk, bad pages, bad schema, empty) and the rows they must map to.

acceptance.criterion: Every fixture maps to the expected rows or the expected error, deterministically.

work_packages.rollback: Revert; nothing calls the module yet.
notes: The row mapping lives in crates/docmonk-convert/src/ai.rs (docmonk-ai never depends on storage); the mapping cases are asserted in crates/docmonk-convert/tests/it/ai_analysis.rs instead of fixtures/ai_analysis/.

work_packages.title: Anthropic API (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) analysis provider
work_packages.purpose: Analyse files with a Claude API key, sending PDFs and images natively.

tasks.title: AiAnalyzer trait
tasks.details: trait AiAnalyzer: Send + Sync { fn analyze(&self, input: &AnalysisInput) -> Result<AnalysisResult, AnalysisError>; fn identity(&self) -> String; }. AnalysisInput carries the file name, format, bytes or text parts, page count and limits. AnalysisError is classed: Transient (timeout, 429, 5xx, quota), Permanent (invalid output, unsupported format, too large), Auth (401/403, not signed in). Add create_analyzer(cfg, privacy, env) next to create_provider, reusing require_external_ai_allowed.

tasks.title: Messages API with document/image blocks
tasks.details: PDF as a base64 document block, images as image blocks, text-like formats as text. Structured output through a forced tool call whose input_schema is the analysis schema. Use temperature 0 and the configured model (default: the current Sonnet-class model id, chosen with the claude-api reference when implementing). Respect max_file_bytes and the API's own request and page limits; above them, fail with ai_analysis_too_large.

tasks.title: Recorded exchanges
tasks.details: Golden cases: success per format, 401, 429, 500 text, non-JSON, tool call missing, schema-invalid output, connection refused. Record the request body (with base64 elided by hash) and the outcome.

acceptance.criterion: All recorded Anthropic analysis cases replay and match.
Without privacy.external_ai_allowed, create_analyzer refuses before building a client.

work_packages.rollback: Revert; analysis mode is not wired into indexing until E7.
notes: Claude Opus 5.5 rejects forced tool_choice and sampling parameters, so structured output (output_config.format) is used, with anthropic-version 2026-10-21 and server-side refusal fallbacks. The recorded exchanges are asserted inline in crates/docmonk-ai/tests/analysis/cases.rs, part of the golden test binary.

work_packages.title: OpenAI API (OPENAI_API_KEY) analysis provider
work_packages.purpose: Analyse files with a ChatGPT/OpenAI API key.

tasks.title: Responses API with file and image inputs
tasks.details: PDF as an input_file (base64), images as input_image, text-like formats as input_text. Structured output with a strict json_schema response format. Use the configured model, and choose the default when implementing. Never reuse the key for codex (registry note stays).

tasks.title: Recorded exchanges
tasks.details: The same case matrix as E3.

acceptance.criterion: All recorded OpenAI analysis cases replay and match.

work_packages.title: Claude subscription (Pro/Max) through the official claude CLI
work_packages.purpose: Use a Claude subscription without an API key, only through Anthropic's own client, for both analysis and docmonk ask.

tasks.title: claude_code runtime
tasks.details: Run the fixed executable name `claude` from PATH (never a configured path), headless (`-p`), with JSON output, the configured model, no session persistence, no MCP servers, and every tool denied except read-only file reading scoped to a fresh temp directory that holds only a copy of the file under an internal name. Remove ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, the DocMonk key variables and GitHub tokens from the child environment, so only the CLI's own sign-in is used and a subscription is never billed as API usage. Pin the exact flags against the installed CLI version when implementing, and record that version in fixtures.

tasks.title: Error mapping
tasks.details: Not signed in maps to Auth (ai_analysis_not_signed_in); usage limit reached or rate limit maps to Transient (ai_analysis_quota); a malformed or empty result maps to Permanent. Each is mapped by exit status and the JSON result's error fields, never by guessing.

tasks.title: Registry, lifecycle and ask
tasks.details: Registry entry claude_code: display 'Claude via Claude Code (subscription)', auth_modes [claude_subscription], subscription true, beta true, cloud_egress true, a new field analysis: true. Add to SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDERS. docmonk ai login/logout claude_code defer to the CLI's own commands; ai status reports signed-in state without secrets. Also implement AiProvider for docmonk ask.

tasks.title: Fake runtime tests
tasks.details: An OS-pipe fake `claude` on PATH: success, not signed in, usage limit, malformed JSON, timeout, and an assertion that the child environment held no API key.

acceptance.criterion: The fake-runtime cases pass, including the stripped-environment assertion.
The owner confirms the invocation stays within the subscription's terms (official CLI only).

notes: Anthropic consumer terms allow a Pro/Max subscription only through Anthropic's own clients; driving the official claude CLI headless follows the existing codex/copilot pattern. The plan never reads or reuses its credentials.
The CLI is found by fixed name on PATH; tests point a CliOptions search path at a fake claude instead of mutating the process environment (unsafe is forbidden).

work_packages.title: ChatGPT subscription analysis through the codex runtime
work_packages.purpose: Reuse the existing codex app-server provider to analyse files with a ChatGPT plan.

tasks.title: Analysis turns over app-server
tasks.details: A new thread per file in the same isolated initialize, with a read-only sandbox, no approvals and no network for tools. Text-like formats go inline; images go as the runtime's image input; PDFs follow decision D2. Ask for the analysis JSON in the final message and validate it with E2.

tasks.title: Error mapping and exchanges
tasks.details: Reuse the existing quota, sign-in and policy mapping to classed AnalysisError, and keep refusing API-key auth modes. Add scripted exchanges for success, quota, signed out, an incomplete turn and invalid JSON.

acceptance.criterion: Scripted codex analysis exchanges replay, and every message sent is recorded.

notes: The codex adapter now speaks the documented app-server protocol (thread/start, turn/start, account/read, device-code login), with approvals never and a read-only sandbox restricted to a private directory. PDFs go as rendered page images (localImage), per the revised D2.

work_packages.title: AI analysis document processor (the bypass)
work_packages.purpose: When documents.analysis.mode=ai, route every document file to the analyzer instead of docling/OCR/normalize/chunk, with identity, caching, limits and failure codes.

tasks.title: Select the processor in registry_with
tasks.details: With mode=native, nothing changes. With mode=ai, r.document is an AiDocumentProcessor built from create_analyzer. Build the analyzer once at index start, so the privacy and not-configured errors stop the run before any file (exit 8 / 3).

tasks.title: Build identity
tasks.details: converter_version = ai-analysis.1+<provider>+<model>+<prompt sha256[..12]>+schema.<n> (+eml-attachments when on); chunker_version gains an ai marker. Any change of mode, provider, model, prompt or schema rebuilds every document. Native identity stays byte-identical.

tasks.title: Prepare: input, limits, cache
tasks.details: detect_format; enforce max_file_bytes and documents.max_pages (page count only, no text read); build the AnalysisInput per D1. Look up the ConversionCache by content hash plus identity; on a miss, call the analyzer and store only validated results. Bound the calls in flight with documents.analysis.concurrency.

tasks.title: Failure semantics (no fallback)
tasks.details: Map AnalysisError to ProcessError codes ai_analysis_failed, ai_analysis_quota, ai_analysis_timeout, ai_analysis_not_signed_in, ai_analysis_invalid_output, ai_analysis_unsupported_format and ai_analysis_too_large. Transient errors set transient=true per D5, so the next index retries. The file gets no document or chunk rows.

tasks.title: Email attachments
tasks.details: Split the MIME envelope natively (it is transport, not analysis). With email_attachments on, analyse each attachment as its own AI call, with the same provenance rows. A failed attachment is counted as failed and does not fail its email, as today.

tasks.title: Processor tests
tasks.details: Use a scripted AiAnalyzer: the corpus indexes; a cache hit makes zero calls; each error code is recorded; the privacy refusal makes zero calls; an identity change rebuilds; mode=native is unchanged.

acceptance.criterion: With mode=ai and a scripted analyzer, no docling, OCR, normalizer or chunker code runs for documents (asserted by a counting converter).
Re-indexing an unchanged corpus makes zero analyzer calls and produces identical rows.

work_packages.rollback: Revert; mode=ai then fails config with a clear message, or the flag is hidden until re-landed.

work_packages.title: Storage fields and AI code references in the linker
work_packages.purpose: Store what the model adds (summary, keywords, extracted_by, code references) on both backends, and turn verified references into links.

requires.description: OpenSearch 2.17 on :9201 and Elasticsearch 8.15 on :9202 (the service containers of .github/workflows/rust.yml)

tasks.title: Document fields
tasks.details: DocumentRow gains summary, keywords and extracted_by (null for native). SQLite schema and server mappings are updated per ADR 0032: a clean-slate rebuild, with nothing that reads earlier stores. Summary and keywords are indexed into the lexical projection with a low field weight. Superseded: no schema change (see notes); summary and keywords go into embedding text.

tasks.title: Code references as link candidates
tasks.details: Store the model's code_references per chunk. The linker turns one into a link only when it resolves exactly to an existing entity, path or route through the existing canonical matcher, with a distinct link source ai_reference and a confidence below explicit/manual links. Unresolved references are dropped and counted.

tasks.title: Provenance in results
tasks.details: search/explore/evidence JSON and text output show extracted_by on AI chunks; ask's evidence prompt keeps its fixed key order and adds the field. Superseded: provenance is the file converter_version shown by documents/status.

acceptance.criterion: AI documents round-trip identically on SQLite, OpenSearch and Elasticsearch.
Only references that resolve to an existing entity become links.

work_packages.rollback: Revert; a clean-slate rebuild restores the previous schema.
notes: No schema change: a schema bump would force every user to reset and reindex even with AI off. Summary and keywords go into each chunk embedding text, provenance is the file converter_version, and code references are kept only when their quote and name occur in the chunk, which the unchanged linker already resolves against real entities. Server and local schemas stay compatible.

decisions.question: Claude and OpenAI APIs ingest PDF, images and text natively, but not DOCX/PPTX/XLSX/ODF/EPUB. How should those formats reach the model?
options: Unpack the zip container and send its XML/HTML parts as text (no interpretation, the model does all analysis)
Convert them natively to Markdown first and send that (partly defeats the bypass)
decisions.recommendation: Unpack the container and send the raw parts (document.xml, slides, sheets with shared strings, content.xml, EPUB XHTML), with images as image inputs up to a cap.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the bypass real: DocMonk does no structural analysis, it only opens the zip. The model still sees all content and markup.
decisions.decision: Unzip Office/OpenDocument/EPUB and send their content XML/HTML members as text (accepted as recommended).

decisions.question: The codex runtime takes text and images but has no native PDF input. How are PDFs analysed with a ChatGPT subscription?
options: Render PDF pages to images and send them (needs a pure-Rust renderer, which costs more tokens)
Fail PDFs on codex with ai_analysis_unsupported_format and recommend the openai key or claude_code
Send the PDF text layer as text (native extraction, breaks the bypass)
decisions.recommendation: Fail PDFs on codex in this plan and document it. Revisit page rendering once a pinned pure-Rust renderer is chosen.
decisions.rationale: Matches 'fail the file' and adds no heavy dependency. Claude subscription and both API keys handle PDFs natively.
decisions.decision: Revised by the owner: ChatGPT reads PDFs. codex gets each PDF as locally rendered page images (hayro, pure Rust), in order, within documents.max_pages; PNG/JPEG images go as they are.

decisions.question: The model decides the chunks. What if a chunk exceeds the embedding model's token budget?
options: Split it deterministically with the existing tokenizer, keeping heading path and pages
Reject the file as invalid output
Store it as is and truncate the embedding
decisions.rationale: It is a length guard, not analysis. Rejecting would fail large tables often, and truncating loses searchable text.
decisions.decision: Split an over-budget chunk with the bundled tokenizer, keeping heading path and pages (accepted as recommended).

decisions.question: Should analysis have its own provider settings or reuse ai.* (used by docmonk ask)?
decisions.rationale: Analysis wants a cheap, high-throughput model with file input. Ask may use another provider, and changing ask must never rebuild the index.

decisions.question: Are quota, rate-limit and timeout failures permanent or retried on the next index?
options: Transient: recorded as failed now, retried on the next index or watcher pass
decisions.recommendation: Transient for quota/rate-limit/timeout/5xx; permanent for invalid output, unsupported format and too large.
decisions.rationale: Subscriptions hit usage windows routinely; files should index once allowance returns without a manual touch.
decisions.decision: Quota, timeout, provider and sign-in failures are transient; the rest permanent (accepted as recommended).

decisions.question: Global flag only, or also per-source overrides (for example AI for scanned contracts, native for wikis)?
decisions.recommendation: Global only now; a per-source override is a follow-up.
decisions.rationale: Matches the storage.mode shape you asked for and keeps the identity and status simple for the first release.

risks.risk: The model paraphrases or invents text, so a citation points to words not in the file.
risks.mitigation: The prompt requires verbatim text in chunk.text (paraphrase only in summary/embedding_text); extracted_by is shown on every AI citation; the live report measures the verbatim ratio against native text.

risks.risk: Subscription use outside the provider's terms, or a subscription silently billed as API usage.
risks.mitigation: Official clients only (claude CLI, codex runtime), fixed executable names, no credential reuse, API-key variables stripped from children, and owner review on E5/E6.

risks.risk: Cost and time: a large corpus means thousands of model calls, and subscriptions hit usage windows.
risks.mitigation: Content-hash cache, bounded concurrency, max_file_bytes and max_pages limits, transient retries (D5), ai analyze to preview, and a clear warning on switch.

risks.risk: Non-determinism: the same file yields different chunks on a rebuild.
risks.mitigation: Temperature 0, cached results reused across runs and rebuilds with the same identity; only a deliberate mode/provider/model/prompt change re-analyses.
Off by default; privacy.external_ai_allowed is required and checked before the run; secret redaction (ADR 0042) is reported in docs as not applied to file bytes sent for analysis; UI warning.

risks.risk: CLI and runtime flag or output drift (claude, codex) breaks the subscription providers.
risks.mitigation: Pin and record the tested versions; doctor reports the version; fake-runtime tests pin the parsing; errors map to clear not-signed-in or invalid-output codes.

stop_and_ask_when: A decision D1-D6 blocks the next step; present the evidence and the recommendation.
A change would alter native extraction output, identity or a protected fixture.
The claude or codex CLI cannot be driven with the isolation E5/E6 require (tools off, no credential env, read-only temp dir).
A secret, signed-in account or cluster listed under requires is not available.
The work package's executor is human, or it is claude_code_then_human_review and the PR is open.
pr_report: Work package id and title in the PR title.
Proof that native parity holds (native_parity output).
Decisions relied on and their recorded answers.
execution.status_updates: On every PR open and merge, update the work package status, tasks[].done, acceptance[].met and pr, append a progress_log entry, and run commands.validate_plan.

progress_log.summary: Plan, D1-D6 decided by the owner, E1-E9 implemented on the PR branch; dependency advisories cleared (docling 2.67.1, rusqlite 0.41, chrono removed, Rust 1.92).
Docs and the ignored live harness are in; the live report needs the owner's keys or signed-in accounts (commands.ai_live).
D2 revised: ChatGPT (codex) analyses PDFs as rendered page images; codex adapter moved to the official app-server protocol.

agent_prompt: Implement plans/ai-file-analysis.json in https://github.com/gzarog/DocMonk. It follows plans/plan.schema.json; read both fully, then inspect current main (the plan was written against 710200a) and adapt where the code has moved. Work in execution.order, starting with execution.start_with, one roadmap/ branch and one PR per work package, respecting depends_on. Never change native extraction output: documents.analysis.mode defaults to native and must stay byte-identical. With mode=ai, documents bypass docling/OCR/normalize/chunk/metadata entirely, failures fail the file with an ai_analysis_* code and never fall back to native. Subscriptions are used only through the official claude CLI and codex runtime, never by reading their credentials. Do only tasks whose executor is not human; for claude_code_then_human_review, open the PR and stop for review; for claude_code_with_cluster, use the service containers from .github/workflows/rust.yml. Obey policy.protected_paths and execution.stop_and_ask_when. Never decide D1-D6 yourself. Report each PR as execution.pr_report says, and update status fields and progress_log as execution.status_updates says, validating with commands.validate_plan.
